shape.name: Shape C — Test-Teach-Test
shape.description: Students are tested on error recognition first, teacher clarifies rules for problematic items, then freer production follows.
shape.pedagogical_justification: Students already have implicit knowledge of capitalisation and punctuation rules from prior exposure. The diagnostic test (Task 1) reveals which specific rules they struggle with. The teacher then clarifies only the problematic patterns (Task 2), followed by a freer writing task (Task 3) where students apply the rules in a paragraph.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
21 July, 2026
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B1
Lesson Shape:
C (Test-Teach-Test)
Materials:
Punctuation & Capitalisation Workshop worksheet, slideshow, exercise books
Assessment:
Error correction answer key (Task 1), rule explanations (Task 2), written paragraph (Task 3)
Systems:
Punctuation, Capitalisation

stages.stage_aim: To activate students' awareness of their own writing errors and frame the lesson value.
procedure: Display the title slide: 'How can I make my writing less messy?' — elicit responses.
Show the 'Why is this lesson important?' slide. Read the bullet points. Ask: 'Do you make these mistakes in your writing?'
State the objective: today we will fix punctuation and capitalisation errors.

stages.stage_aim: To focus students on the target language through a concrete example (i → I).
procedure: Show the Example slide (auto-animate: i → I).
Ask: 'What is wrong here?' Elicit that 'i' should be capitalised.
Press right arrow to show the corrected version with yellow highlight on 'I'.
CCQ: 'Why is i wrong?' (The pronoun I is always capitalised.)

stages.stage_aim: To diagnostically assess which punctuation and capitalisation errors students can identify.
procedure: Show the 'Task 1 — Recognise' transition slide (red).
Review instructions: Circle each error, write the correction above.
Point out that Question 1 has 2 errors — demonstrate the process.
Start the 8-minute timer. Students work individually on the worksheet.
After the timer, go through each question one at a time using the auto-animate answer slides. Students mark their own work.

stages.stage_aim: To clarify the rules behind the error patterns.
procedure: Show the 'Task 2 — Recall' slide (red). Review instructions: explain each rule in one complete sentence.
Start the 5-minute timer. Students write rule explanations for the 4 items (comma spacing, Anna, We/The, however).
After the timer, review each rule slide. For each: read the rule, ask CCQs.
Key rules: (1) No space before a comma, (2) Commas around extra information about a person, (3) Comma after introductory phrases + lowercase, (4) Semicolon before 'however' + comma after.

stages.stage_aim: To give students freer written practice applying all rules.
procedure: Show the 'Task 3 — Use' slide (red). Explain: write up to 70 words about a fun day with family or friends.
Review the checklist: sentence starting with 'while' or 'even though', extra info in commas, comma before and/but, correct use of 'however'.
Start the 8-minute timer. Circulate and provide support.
Collect paragraphs for assessment.

metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: Students will review rules for capitalisation, comma usage, and semicolons with 'however'.
answer_key: Q5: Add commas around 'who lives next door' + Teacher→teacher
Q9: Add semicolon before 'however' + comma after
R1: No space before a comma; space after.
R2: Commas around extra information about a person (appositives).
R3: After introductory phrase, comma + lowercase letter.
